workflows.name: IT Operations & Helpdesk Support

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow notification of "contacts IT Helpdesk via phone, email, or self-service portal" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-create of "creates support ticket" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "routes ticket based on category" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: IT Helpdesk Lead review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Geographic coverage gap**: 200 stores + 4 DCs across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao stretch the 5-person regional field-technician team (one per major island region — Mindanao, Visayas, South Luzon, Metro Manila, North/Central Luzon — per the IT operating model's Field & End-User Services team); remote island stores may still wait 1–3 days for on-site repair, requiring regional contractor partnerships

- **P1 SLA pressure**: A single store with all POS terminals down triggers a 4-hour resolution SLA; if the issue requires on-site presence and the nearest IT field staff is on another island, SLA is at high risk of breach

- **Recurring issues masking systemic problems**: High ticket volume (800–1,200/month) can mask underlying infrastructure or training problems; without root cause trend analysis, helpdesk becomes a reactive fire-fighting operation

- **Change window conflicts**: Tuesday/Thursday 22:00–02:00 maintenance windows may overlap with 24-hour or extended-hour store operations, risking unintended disruption to late-night inventory or ecommerce processing
Severity & SLA Matrix: | Severity | Definition | Examples | Response SLA | Resolution SLA |
Staffing Implication: - **4–5 Helpdesk Agents (Tier 1)**: handle ~800–1,200 tickets/month ÷ 20 working days = ~40–60/day. At ~10 min average per ticket = ~7–10 hours/day. With shifts and coverage, 4–5 agents needed.
- **3–4 IT Specialists (Tier 2)**: Application support, infrastructure, retail IT, security. Specialists handle ~30% of tickets that Tier 1 cannot resolve = ~240–360/month.

- **5 Regional IT Field Technicians** (one per major island region, per the IT operating model's Field & End-User Services team): physical site visits for hardware issues across 200 stores + 4 DCs. Estimated 50–80 on-site visits/month across the Philippines, absorbed with regional coverage and travel time.
- **1 IT Helpdesk Lead**: manages helpdesk operations, SLA compliance, change management.
- **Total IT**: IT team of ~50 (per profile §3.3), including 5 helpdesk agents, 4 specialists, 5 regional field technicians, and 1 lead across infrastructure, applications, data, security, and BI.
System Touchpoints: - IT ticket management: create, route, escalate, resolve, close with full audit trail (W48.2–10)
- Auto-routing by issue category to specialist queues (W48.3)
- SLA timer per severity level with auto-escalation at 75% of SLA threshold (W48.4–9)
- Remote desktop / diagnostic tool integration (W48.4, 7)
- Knowledge base / self-service portal for common issues (W48.1)
- Change request workflow with classification and approval (W48 change management)
- Maintenance window scheduling (W48 change 4)
- Ticket analytics dashboard: volume, SLA compliance, MTTR, top issues by location (W48.11)

- SLA breach escalation protocol: (a) single P1 SLA miss (resolution > 4 hours): IT Helpdesk Lead conducts immediate root cause analysis and documents corrective action; (b) 2 consecutive P1 SLA misses on same issue category: Helpdesk Lead escalates to CIO with remediation plan within 24 hours; CIO reviews staffing, tooling, or vendor support adequacy; (c) 3 or more P1 SLA misses within 30 days (any category): CIO presents incident review to CEO with systemic improvement plan (may include additional headcount, vendor escalation, or infrastructure investment); (d) P2/P3 SLA misses trending > 20% breach rate for 2 consecutive months: Helpdesk Lead initiates category-specific improvement (process change, training, or automation); (e) all SLA breaches tracked in monthly ticket analytics dashboard with trend analysis and root cause classification; SLA performance included in IT team's quarterly performance review (W48)

- IT asset tracking: system maintains asset register for all IT equipment (POS terminals, RF devices, servers, networking equipment, laptops, tablets) with location assignment, warranty status, maintenance history, and lifecycle status; supports IT asset planning and budgeting (cross-reference W21 for capex, W39 for disposal)
- Integration with W5G (offline POS recovery), W16 (new store IT setup), W43 (employee separation — account deactivation)
Time Estimate: - Ticket creation and Tier 1 resolution: 5–20 min/ticket; Tier 2 specialist: 15–60 min/ticket; Tier 3 vendor escalation: vendor-dependent (hours to days)
- Change management: 10–15 min/review + maintenance window execution per change
- Monthly analytics review: 2 hours/month
- Overall: ~800–1,200 tickets/month require ~130–200 staff-hours/month across Tier 1–3

steps.activity: User contacts IT Helpdesk via phone, email, or self-service portal; describes issue with system, hardware, network, or access
Helpdesk Agent creates support ticket: user, location, device, issue category, severity (see matrix below), description

System auto-routes ticket based on category: (a) POS/retail → Retail IT support queue, (b) network/connectivity → Infrastructure queue, (c) ERP/application → Applications queue, (d) hardware → Hardware support queue, (e) access/permissions → Security queue
**Tier 1 — Remote resolution**: Helpdesk Agent attempts to resolve remotely (password reset, configuration fix, user guidance, system restart)
If Tier 1 resolves: ticket closed with resolution code; user confirms
If Tier 1 unresolved: ticket escalated to Tier 2 (specialist) with diagnostic notes; SLA timer restarts per severity
**Tier 2 — Specialist resolution**: IT specialist investigates; may require remote session, configuration change, or system-level fix
If Tier 2 requires on-site presence (hardware failure, network cabling, POS terminal replacement): ticket assigned to IT Field Support with scheduled site visit
**Tier 3 — Vendor / escalation**: if issue requires vendor support (POS software bug, ERP vendor support, hardware warranty claim), IT engages vendor; tracks vendor response SLA
Resolution confirmed by user; ticket closed; system logs resolution time, root cause category, and recurring issue flag
Monthly: IT Helpdesk Lead reviews ticket analytics: volume by category, resolution rate by tier, SLA compliance, mean time to resolution, top recurring issues per location
IT team member submits change request: description, affected systems, risk assessment, rollback plan, planned window

IT Helpdesk Lead reviews and classifies: (a) standard change (pre-approved, low risk — e.g., password policy update), (b) normal change (requires review and approval — e.g., POS software patch), (c) emergency change (unplanned, critical fix — e.g., security vulnerability patch)
Normal changes: CIO approves; emergency changes: CIO verbal approval with post-hoc documentation; standard changes: auto-approved per catalog
Change executed during maintenance window (typically Tuesday/Thursday 22:00–02:00 or Sunday 00:00–04:00 to avoid peak hours)
Post-change verification: IT confirms system health; Helpdesk monitors for related ticket spikes in next 24 hours

workflows.name: System Upgrade & New Entity Integration Testing

Automation Opportunity: - auto-integration; real-time data sync
- auto-report generation and distribution
- workflow automation; rule-based routing
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Business user availability**: Validation and testing require department experts (Category Managers, Cost Accountant, Payroll Officer) who must perform these checks alongside daily operations
- **Financial reconciliation**: Reconciling trial balances and ledgers post-upgrade or post-onboarding is critical to prevent cascading errors in subsequent financial reporting
Staffing Implication: - **Business user time**: Validation and testing effort is absorbed within existing headcount. Testing tasks are scheduled during off-peak hours to minimize disruption to steady-state operations.
System Touchpoints: - Data migration validation workbench: compare migrated data to source with side-by-side display and discrepancy flagging (W73.1–7)
- Parallel-run comparison reports: payroll output comparison, trial balance comparison, Z-report comparison, inventory balance comparison (W73.8–11)
- UAT test case management: scripted test cases with pass/fail tracking and defect logging (W73.12)
- Release readiness sign-off workflow with department-level approval (W73.13)
- Integration with all operational workflows (each workflow validated during UAT), W384 (ERP Environment Management), W385 (Data Migration Operational Lifecycle)
Time Estimate: - Upgrade testing and validation: ~20–40 hours of business user effort per major release cycle
- Parallel-run testing per upgrade: ~10–20 hours
- UAT per major release: ~10–20 hours

steps.activity: **Item master validation**: Merchandise Planners verify updated or new SKU data — sample 100–500 SKUs; confirm item description, unit of measure, cost, SRP, category assignment, and attributes match database standards; report discrepancies to IT for correction

**Customer master validation**: AR Clerks verify sample of trade/corporate accounts — confirm credit limits, payment terms, and VAT treatment classification; Loyalty Manager verifies sample of loyalty accounts — points balance, tier status, and contact info
**Vendor master validation**: Buyers verify sample of vendors — confirm payment terms, lead times, bank details, and tax classification

**Inventory balance validation**: Cost Accountant and DC/Store Supervisors verify opening inventory balances for new locations or after system migration — reconcile quantities and values (WAC) to baseline records; identify discrepancies > 1% by value

**Financial validation**: Controller and Chief Accountant verify trial balance and ledger integration for new entities or post-upgrade — GL account mappings, open AP/AR invoices, fixed asset register, and bank connections
**Employee master validation**: HR Head verifies employee data for new locations or post-upgrade — confirm salary, tax status, statutory deduction registration, and organizational assignment
All validation exceptions logged in IT ticket tracker; corrected and re-validated until zero material discrepancies

**Payroll parallel run**: for upgrades affecting the payroll engine, Payroll Officer runs payroll in both sandbox (upgrade test) and production environments; compares output per employee; discrepancies > PHP 1 flagged and resolved
**Close process parallel run**: for upgrades affecting accounting rules, Chief Accountant performs test close steps in sandbox; compares trial balance and key reconciliation outputs to production

**POS upgrade testing**: for POS software updates or new store openings, Cashiers process test transactions on designated terminal in sandbox or staging mode; Store Manager compares test Z-reports against expectations
**Inventory transaction testing**: stock associates execute key inventory transactions (receipt, transfer, count, sales deduction) in sandbox; Cost Accountant validates ending balance calculations

**User acceptance testing (UAT)**: before major upgrades, designated power users from each department execute scripted UAT test cases covering critical workflows; all test cases must pass with zero critical defects
**Sign-off**: after successful UAT, Department Heads sign off on release readiness; Controller signs off on financial accuracy; CFO gives final go-live approval

workflows.name: Business Intelligence & Data Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "check if an existing report already covers the need" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "logic, filters, refresh frequency" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Data quality monitoring" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: RPT-001 through RPT-010 define reporting requirements — executive dashboards, store P&L, sales analytics, inventory reports, ad-hoc reporting, and scheduled distribution. W35 defines the management reporting rhythm. However, there is no workflow governing the BI layer itself: how reports and dashboards are created, maintained, and retired; how data quality is monitored; how ad-hoc requests are prioritized; who owns which data domain; and how the data dictionary and business rules are maintained. Without BI governance, reports proliferate (creating "Excel hell"), data definitions diverge across departments, and the same metric shows different values in different reports — undermining trust in data-driven decisions at PHP 62.3B scale.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: BI Manager / Data Analyst review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **"Excel hell" proliferation**: Without strict governance, departments create local Excel reports that diverge from official BI definitions; the same metric (e.g., gross margin) can show different values across departments, eroding trust in data

- **Ad-hoc request backlog**: 50–100 requests/month can overwhelm 2–3 Data Analysts, especially if executives submit expedited requests that preempt scheduled work; backlog leads to shadow reporting by departments

- **Data definition disputes**: When Finance, Merchandising, and Supply Chain disagree on metric calculations (e.g., should returns be deducted before or after margin calculation?), the BI Manager lacks formal authority to resolve disputes — only the governance meeting provides a forum (with escalation to W474 DGC if unresolved)

- **Dashboard retirement resistance**: Users often resist retirement of dashboards even when usage analytics show zero logins in 90+ days; political pressure to keep unused reports alive wastes maintenance effort
Staffing Implication: - **1 BI Manager** (within IT team of ~50): manages BI platform, governance, and team. This role is implied by RPT requirements but not formalized.

- **2–3 Data Analysts** (within IT team): develop reports, manage data quality, maintain data dictionary. At ~50–100 requests/month × 4–8 hours each for new reports, plus ongoing maintenance = ~2–3 full-time equivalents. Redeployed from existing IT team or new hires within planned IT headcount.
- **No incremental headcount beyond planned IT team.**
System Touchpoints: - BI report request portal with classification, priority, and SLA tracking (W113.1)
- Report development standards and publishing workflow with approval gates (W113.2)
- Automated daily data quality checks: completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency (W113.3)
- Data quality scorecard by domain with trend tracking (W113.3)
- Dashboard usage analytics with login frequency, view count, and load time metrics (W113.4)
- Dashboard retirement workflow with 30-day user notification and archiving (W113.4)
- Master data dictionary with metric definitions, domain ownership, calculation logic, and source mapping (W113.5)
- Role-based access control for reports and dashboards per NFR-007 (W113.7)

- Integration with W35 (management reporting — reports consumed in reporting rhythm), W48 (IT helpdesk — BI tool support), W53 (data privacy — customer data in reports), W55 (DR — BI system failover), W73 (system upgrades — BI data source validation post-upgrade), W474 (Enterprise Data Governance Council — dispute escalation and policy arbitration)
Time Estimate: - Ad-hoc report request triage: 15 min/request; new report development: 4–8 hours; modification: 1–2 hours
- Daily data quality alert review: 30 min/day; monthly data quality scorecard: 2 hours/month
- Quarterly dashboard lifecycle review: 4 hours/quarter
- Data dictionary maintenance: ~4 hours/month ongoing
- Monthly BI governance meeting: 1 hour/month
- Access control management: 30 min/month + 4 hours/quarter (review)
- Annual BI roadmap: 8 hours/year
- Total ongoing BI governance overhead: ~15–20 hours/month for BI Manager + ~40–80 hours/month for Data Analysts on report delivery

steps.activity: **Ad-hoc report request intake**: Department Head or Manager submits report request via BI request portal: (a) request description (what data is needed, for what purpose), (b) desired format (dashboard, scheduled report, one-time extract), (c) urgency (standard 5-day SLA, expedited 2-day SLA with Department Head justification, immediate — routed to BI Manager for triage), (d) intended audience (who will consume the report); BI Manager triages daily: (e) check if an existing report already covers the need (duplicate detection), (f) classify as: reuse existing, modify existing, or create new, (g) assign to Data Analyst with priority and deadline

**Report development and approval**: Data Analyst develops report per request: (a) uses approved data sources and definitions from data dictionary (step 5), (b) validates output against known data points (reconciliation with source system), (c) creates report with appropriate visualization and documentation (data source, calculation logic, filters, refresh frequency), (d) BI Manager reviews for accuracy, performance (query execution time < 30 seconds per NFR-004), and adherence to report design standards, (e) requestor reviews and confirms report meets need, (f) BI Manager publishes report to appropriate audience group with access controls

**Data quality monitoring**: System runs automated daily data quality checks across critical data domains: (a) **Completeness**: are all expected records present? (e.g., every store should have daily sales data), (b) **Accuracy**: do totals reconcile? (e.g., sum of store sales = consolidated total), (c) **Timeliness**: is data current? (e.g., POS data loaded within 30 minutes of transaction), (d) **Consistency**: do cross-system metrics agree? (e.g., ERP inventory = WMS inventory), (e) anomalies generate data quality alerts to BI Manager and IT; BI Manager investigates and coordinates with IT for resolution; monthly: BI Manager generates data quality scorecard by domain (target: ≥ 98% quality score)

**Dashboard lifecycle management**: Quarterly: BI Manager reviews all active dashboards: (a) **Usage analytics**: which dashboards are actively used (login frequency, view count)? — dashboards not accessed in 90 days flagged for retirement, (b) **Performance**: which dashboards have slow load times or query timeouts? — prioritize for optimization, (c) **Accuracy**: have underlying data sources changed (new GL accounts, new locations, new item categories) that require dashboard updates?, (d) **Retirement**: deprecated dashboards archived (not deleted) with retirement date and reason; users notified 30 days before retirement

**Data dictionary and business rules maintenance**: BI Manager maintains master data dictionary: (a) **Metric definitions**: every KPI used in reports has a single documented definition (e.g., "Gross Margin = (Revenue − COGS) ÷ Revenue × 100; Revenue = net of returns; COGS = weighted average cost"), (b) **Data domain ownership**: each data domain has a designated owner (e.g., Finance owns financial metrics, Merchandising owns sales metrics, Supply Chain owns inventory metrics), (c) **Calculation logic**: documented and version-controlled for every report metric, (d) **Source system mapping**: every metric traced to its source system field, (e) updates to data dictionary require BI Manager approval and are logged with effective date and reason

**Monthly BI governance meeting**: BI Manager convenes monthly BI governance meeting with Department Head representatives: (a) review data quality scorecard, (b) review open report requests and backlog, (c) discuss upcoming reporting needs (new metrics, new data sources, organizational changes), (d) resolve data definition disputes (when departments disagree on metric calculation; unresolved disputes are escalated to the Enterprise Data Governance Council per W474), (e) review report usage and identify opportunities to consolidate overlapping reports, (f) approve data dictionary changes

**Access control and security**: BI Manager manages report and dashboard access per NFR-007 security requirements: (a) reports containing financial data restricted to Finance and authorized roles, (b) store-level P&L visible to Store Manager (own store only), Regional Manager (stores in region), and COO (all stores), (c) customer data in reports masked per RA 10173 data privacy requirements (W53), (d) access changes logged with approver and reason; quarterly: BI Manager reviews access control list for appropriateness

**Annual BI roadmap**: CIO and BI Manager prepare annual BI roadmap: (a) planned new reports and dashboards based on business priorities, (b) technology upgrades (BI tool versions, data warehouse performance), (c) self-service BI enablement — train power users in Department Heads to create own reports using governed data sets, (d) data integration roadmap — new data sources to onboard (3PL tracking data, ecommerce behavioral data, vendor portal data), (e) budget for BI tools, training, and external consulting

workflows.name: Software Development & Change Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Document functional and technical specs" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Verify code in QA environment" (replaces manual Step 3).
- System auto-test of "User Acceptance Testing" (replaces manual Step 4).
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: Application Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **BIR CAS re-registration trigger**: Major ERP system changes (version upgrades, new modules, platform changes) require re-registration with BIR per W54A step 10; the 2–6 month BIR processing time can delay deployment of critical system improvements

- **UAT bottlenecks**: Business users (Category Managers, Store Managers, Finance staff) must test changes alongside their operational duties; UAT often becomes the critical-path delay in the release cycle, especially during peak retail periods (Q4 holidays, monthly close)

- **Rollback risk on integrated systems**: With 50+ active enterprise integrations (W257), a change to one module (e.g., pricing engine) can cascade into POS, ecommerce, loyalty, and BI; incomplete rollback plans for interconnected changes can cause extended outages; mitigated by the Application Manager review and approval gate

- **Weekly release cadence strain**: 5–10 changes/week with a small development team means overlapping release cycles; if a hotfix is needed while a major change is in UAT, prioritization conflicts and environment contention can delay both
Staffing Implication: - **Application Manager (1)**: manages development team, CAB process, and release schedule. Full-time role within IT team of ~50.
- **Business Analysts (1–2)**: requirements gathering and specification documentation per change. ~3–5 days per change × 5–10 changes/week = shared across 1–2 BAs.
- **Developers (3–4)**: code changes at 1–2 weeks per change with 5–10 changes/week pipeline. 3–4 developers can handle the weekly cadence with overlapping sprints.
- **QA Team (2)**: unit/integration testing at 2–3 days per change. Absorbed within IT team.
- **CAB (Change Advisory Board)**: CIO + App Manager + 1 rotating Department Head. ~1 hour/week. Absorbed.
- **No incremental headcount beyond planned IT team of ~50.**
System Touchpoints: - Change Management / Jira tracking for software development lifecycle (requirements, development, testing, deployment)
- Automated deployment / CI-CD pipeline logs with rollback capability
- Sandbox/Dev, QA, and Production environment segregation with promotion controls
- UAT sign-off workflow with business user approval gate
- Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval log with risk assessment and rollback plan
- Release notes and version tracking per module

- Integration with W48 (helpdesk — production incidents from releases), W73 (system upgrades — testing system changes during upgrades), W132 (BIR CAS — major system changes may require re-registration per W54A step 10)
Time Estimate: - Requirement analysis: 3–5 days per change
- Development: 1–2 weeks per change (simple bug fixes: 1–2 days; medium features: 1 week; major features: 2+ weeks)
- QA testing: 2–3 days per change
- UAT: 2–5 days per change (depends on business user availability)
- CAB review: 1 hour/change
- Deployment: 2 hours/change in maintenance window
- End-to-end cycle: 2–4 weeks for standard changes; emergency changes: 1–2 days

workflows.name: Employee IT Provisioning & Access Lifecycle Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-request of "request" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "account, company email, and employee ID link" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-assign of "Assign ERP roles" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-54 (prevent unauthorized employee master data changes.)
- operational: IT Infrastructure Manager review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ghost account exposure**: With ~6,762 employees and high turnover in retail (estimated 15–20% annual turnover), delayed de-provisioning creates "ghost accounts" that former employees can use to access sensitive systems; a single missed de-provisioning can be a data privacy breach under RA 10173

- **Role creep on transfers**: When employees transfer between departments or stores, old permissions are often added to rather than replaced; over time, long-tenured employees accumulate access far beyond their current role requirement

- **New store opening provisioning surge**: Opening 10–15 new stores/year (W16) means onboarding 350–525 new employees in compressed timeframes (typically within 1–2 weeks per store opening); IT Helpdesk must prioritize provisioning batches without delaying store go-live

- **Remote store de-provisioning**: When an employee at a remote VisMin store separates, hardware retrieval requires shipping or a field visit; the physical asset may not be recovered for days or weeks after the account is disabled
Staffing Implication: - **IT Helpdesk**: 100–150 provisioning events/month × ~1.75 hours each (45 min identity + 1 hour hardware) = ~175–260 hours/month. Distributed across 4–5 helpdesk agents = ~35–52 hours/agent/month. Absorbed within W48 helpdesk capacity.
- **IT Infrastructure Manager**: oversees access role mapping standards and RBAC policy. ~2–4 hours/month on role matrix reviews. Absorbed.
- **Security Admin**: monthly ghost account audit at 4 hours/month + quarterly access certification review. Absorbed within IT Security role.
- **No incremental headcount beyond planned IT team of ~50.**
System Touchpoints: - Active Directory / Azure AD integration with HR master for automated provisioning triggers
- ERP role-based access control (RBAC) engine tied to job code master for consistent role mapping
- IT Helpdesk ticketing system (W48) for provisioning and de-provisioning request tracking
- Digital acknowledgment form with electronic signature capture for asset handover
- Automated account deactivation trigger from W43 (employee separation) workflow
- Access certification report for quarterly compliance review (SOX-style, RA 10173)
- Integration with W15 (onboarding — provisioning trigger), W43 (separation — de-provisioning trigger), W48 (helpdesk — access issues), W53 (data privacy — access audit)
Time Estimate: - Identity creation and access role mapping: 45 min/employee (steps 2–3)
- Hardware preparation: 1 hour/employee (step 4)
- Transfer / role change: 30 min/event (step 5)

steps.activity: **Incident Reporting**: Store staff reports POS hardware issue via: (a) IT Helpdesk ticket (W48 P2/P3 priority — POS down at specific terminal impacts checkout capacity but store remains operational with remaining terminals); (b) common issues: (i) receipt printer jam or failure (most frequent, ~40% of incidents), (ii) barcode scanner not reading (laser/CMOS degradation, ~25%), (iii) cash drawer stuck or sensor failure (~15%), (iv) PIN pad / card reader communication error (~10%), (v) touchscreen unresponsive or display failure (~5%), (vi) cable/connector damage (power, network, USB, ~5%)

**Remote Diagnosis**: IT Helpdesk receives ticket and performs remote diagnosis: (a) checks POS terminal status via remote management console; (b) reviews error logs for specific peripheral; (c) attempts remote remediation: (i) restart printer spooler service, (ii) recalibrate barcode scanner, (iii) reset PIN pad communication, (iv) clear cash drawer sensor jam via software; (d) if remote fix successful: close ticket and log resolution; (e) if remote fix unsuccessful: escalate to on-site response

**Spare Part Dispatch or On-Site Visit**: For issues requiring physical intervention: (a) **peripheral swap (most common)**: Helpdesk authorizes Store Manager to swap failed peripheral with store's spare unit (each store maintains 1 spare receipt printer, 1 spare scanner, 1 spare PIN pad per NFR-024 IT asset management); (b) **on-site visit**: if spare swap doesn't resolve or issue is terminal-level (touchscreen, motherboard), IT Support Specialist schedules on-site visit (next business day for P2; same-day for P1 if > 2 terminals down at one store); (c) **central depot repair**: for complex failures, IT Support Specialist ships terminal to central IT depot (Davao HQ or regional hub) for repair

**Repair or Replacement Execution**: IT Support Specialist performs on-site or depot repair: (a) diagnoses hardware failure (component-level: print head, laser diode, touchscreen digitizer, cable connector); (b) if repairable on-site: replace component from IT spare parts inventory (W131 IT asset lifecycle); (c) if unrepairable: replace entire unit from IT asset pool; (d) defective unit tagged for depot repair or disposal per W39; (e) system updated: IT asset register (W131) records asset status change, repair history, and replacement serial number

**Configuration & Testing**: After swap or repair: (a) configure replacement peripheral: pair with POS terminal via Bluetooth/USB, load printer driver, set scanner configuration, configure PIN pad merchant ID and encryption keys; (b) test all functions: print test receipt, scan 5 test barcodes (1D and 2D), process test card transaction (PHP 1.00 authorization and void), open/close cash drawer, verify customer display output; (c) Store Manager confirms terminal operational and signs off ticket

**IT Asset Register Update**: IT Asset Manager updates asset records: (a) replaced peripheral: serial number, date of replacement, reason code, store location, replaced-by IT staff ID; (b) defective unit: tagged for depot repair (status: "In Repair"), disposed (status: "Disposed" per W39), or returned to vendor under warranty (W33 warranty claim per peripheral); (c) asset lifecycle cost tracking: repair cost, downtime hours, replacement cost per terminal/peripheral

**Preventive Maintenance (Quarterly)**: Per PM schedule: (a) IT Support Specialist visits each store quarterly (rotating schedule across 200 stores = ~15 stores/week); (b) per-terminal PM checklist: (i) clean receipt printer print head and paper path, (ii) clean barcode scanner lens and test read rate, (iii) inspect cash drawer rails and sensors, (iv) check PIN pad keypad responsiveness and update firmware, (v) clean touchscreen, (vi) inspect all cables and connectors for wear, (vii) verify UPS battery charge level (critical for W5G offline capability); (c) PM results logged in asset register; issues found during PM create follow-up tickets

**Vendor Warranty & RMA Management**: For peripherals under manufacturer warranty: (a) IT Asset Manager tracks warranty expiration per serial number; (b) for in-warranty failures: initiate RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) with vendor; (c) ship defective unit to vendor; use spare pool unit as replacement; (d) track RMA status and vendor turnaround time; (e) vendor SLA: replacement or repair within 10–15 business days; (f) feed vendor RMA performance into vendor scorecard (W44) for peripheral vendor contract renewal

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review release notes" (replaces manual Step 1).

Background: BuildRight's unified cloud ERP system (supporting 600 POS terminals, 200 stores, 4 DCs, 5 legal entities, and 6,762 users) requires ongoing patch and upgrade management to maintain security, performance, and compliance. ERP vendor releases include: (a) **Critical security patches**: zero-day vulnerabilities, security fixes requiring immediate application; (b) **Monthly minor patches**: bug fixes, regulatory updates (BIR tax table changes, SSS/PhilHealth rate changes), performance improvements; (c) **Quarterly cumulative updates**: feature enhancements, UI updates, integration improvements; (d) **Annual major upgrades**: significant new features, platform changes, database schema updates. W132 covers general software development & change management but does not address the ERP-specific patch and upgrade lifecycle — which requires sandbox testing, regression testing across all modules, coordinated downtime windows, and rollback planning for a system that powers the entire business. Failed patches can take down POS terminals, halt supply chain operations, or corrupt financial data.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: IT — ERP System Administrator review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Downtime impact on 200 stores**: Any ERP downtime affects all 200 stores' ability to process transactions (unless POS is in offline mode W5G); even scheduled downtime on Sundays can impact stores open 7 days a week; failed deployments requiring extended downtime can result in significant revenue loss

- **Customization regression risk**: BuildRight's ERP has significant customizations (BIR tax compliance, Philippine statutory reporting, intercompany workflows, catch-weight processing) that may not be covered by the vendor's standard regression test suite; custom code regression is the highest risk in any patch or upgrade; mitigated by the IT — ERP System Administrator review and approval gate

- **Integration chain failure**: The ERP integrates with 10+ external systems (POS, ecommerce, banks, BIR eFPS, EIS, SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG, 3PL, payment gateways); a patch that changes an API interface can break multiple integrations simultaneously

- **Vendor release cadence pressure**: Cloud ERP vendors may release updates on a fixed cadence that does not align with BuildRight's operational calendar; deferring patches too long creates security exposure, while applying patches during peak retail periods (Christmas, bi-monthly sales) is risky

- **Rollback complexity**: For major upgrades, rollback may not be possible if database schema changes are irreversible; this means a failed major upgrade could require rebuilding from backup, resulting in data loss for transactions processed between backup and rollback
Staffing Implication: - **ERP System Administrator**: ~200–300 hours/year on patch and upgrade management. Significant portion of role.
- **Application Support Team**: ~100–200 hours/year for sandbox testing and post-deployment verification. Absorbed across team.
- **BASIS Team**: ~50–100 hours/year for deployment execution. Absorbed.
- **Key Users (Finance, Supply Chain, HR, Store Ops)**: ~40–80 hours/year for UAT participation. Absorbed with scheduling coordination.
System Touchpoints: - ERP System: patch and upgrade deployment target
- Sandbox Environment (W384): pre-deployment testing
- Change Management System (W132): change request, approval, deployment tracking
- Backup & Recovery System (W382): pre-deployment backup and rollback
- System Monitoring (W380): post-deployment performance monitoring
- Helpdesk System (W48): post-deployment issue tracking

- Integration with W132 (change management), W384 (environment management), W382 (backup), W380 (alert/event management), W48 (helpdesk), W5G (offline POS), W257 (API management), W367 (security operations), W376 (capacity planning)
Time Estimate: - Monthly minor patch: 3–5 days elapsed (4–8 hours IT effort)
- Quarterly cumulative update: 1–2 weeks elapsed (15–25 hours IT effort)
- Critical security patch: 1–3 days elapsed (8–16 hours IT effort)
- Annual major upgrade: 3–6 months planning + 1 week deployment
- **Total annual IT effort**: ~300–500 hours/year for ERP patch and upgrade management

steps.activity: **Release Notification & Impact Assessment**: ERP System Administrator receives vendor release notification: (a) review release notes for: security fixes, functional changes, regulatory updates, deprecated features, integration impacts; (b) assess impact on BuildRight's configuration: customizations, integrations (POS, ecommerce, banks, BIR), modified reports, and custom workflows; (c) classify release impact: **Critical** (security or compliance — apply within SLA), **High** (affects core processes — apply within 2 weeks), **Medium** (feature enhancements — apply next quarterly window), **Low** (cosmetic — defer to next quarterly window); (d) prepare impact assessment report for CIO

**Sandbox Environment Testing**: Application Support Team deploys release to sandbox (non-production) environment: (a) deploy to sandbox environment (W384 — ERP environment management); (b) execute regression test suite: POS transaction flow, AP 3-way match (W7), AR billing (W8), payroll processing (W10), inventory transactions (W3/W4), ecommerce integration (W11/W19), bank integration (W30), BIR EIS transmission (W473), intercompany processing (W14); (c) key users from Finance, Supply Chain, HR, and Store Ops perform user acceptance testing (UAT) on critical workflows; (d) document test results and any issues found

**Customization & Integration Compatibility Check**: Application Support Team verifies: (a) all custom ABAP/SQL code, enhancements, and user exits are compatible with the new release; (b) all integration interfaces (POS, ecommerce, bank, BIR eFPS, EIS, SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG) are compatible; (c) all third-party add-ons and bolt-on solutions are certified for the new release version; (d) all modified reports, forms, and BIR-registered invoice layouts render correctly; (e) if incompatibilities found: work with vendor or internal development (W132) to remediate before production deployment

**Go/No-Go Decision**: IT Manager convenes Go/No-Go meeting: (a) review sandbox test results; (b) review customization and integration compatibility status; (c) assess rollback risk; (d) confirm downtime window availability (per NFR-015 batch processing windows); (e) confirm key user availability for post-deployment validation; (f) make Go/No-Go decision; if Go: confirm deployment date and communicate to stakeholders

**Pre-Deployment Preparation**: ERP System Administrator prepares for deployment: (a) full system backup (W382); (b) verify rollback plan: how to revert to pre-patch version if critical failure occurs; (c) prepare deployment runbook: step-by-step deployment sequence, verification checkpoints, rollback triggers; (d) notify all stakeholders of planned downtime: Store Managers (POS unavailable), Finance (ERP unavailable), DC Operations (WMS unavailable), ecommerce team (ecommerce maintenance mode); (e) coordinate with POS team for offline POS readiness (W5G) during downtime

**Production Deployment**: ERP System Administrator deploys to production: (a) execute deployment during approved downtime window (typically Saturday night/Sunday morning to minimize impact — per NFR-015); (b) monitor deployment progress; (c) verify deployment at each checkpoint; (d) if deployment fails at any checkpoint: execute rollback per runbook; (e) if deployment succeeds: proceed to post-deployment verification

**Post-Deployment Verification**: Application Support Team and Key Users verify production deployment: (a) smoke test critical workflows: POS transaction, AP invoice posting, AR billing, payroll calculation, inventory movement, BIR EIS transmission; (b) verify all integrations are functioning (POS ↔ ERP, ecommerce ↔ ERP, bank ↔ ERP); (c) verify report generation and dashboard rendering; (d) verify POS terminals are connecting and processing transactions; (e) if issues found: triage severity and apply hotfix or execute rollback; (f) if no issues: confirm deployment success and lift downtime

**Post-Deployment Monitoring**: ERP System Administrator monitors for 7 days post-deployment: (a) monitor system performance metrics (response time, batch job duration, database load); (b) monitor error logs for new or unusual errors; (c) monitor user-reported issues via helpdesk (W48); (d) if new issues emerge after deployment: assess whether patch-related and apply fix or escalate to vendor; (e) close release in change management log (W132) after 7-day monitoring period

**Annual Major Upgrade Planning**: For annual major upgrades (additional steps): (a) start planning 3–6 months before vendor target date; (b) conduct comprehensive impact assessment including all modules, customizations, and integrations; (c) negotiate with vendor for BuildRight-specific upgrade timeline (may differ from standard vendor timeline); (d) plan extended sandbox testing period (4–8 weeks); (e) plan extended downtime window (may require 8–24 hours); (f) plan key user training on new features (W51); (g) plan parallel-run period for critical modules if upgrade includes significant functional changes (W73); (h) budget for upgrade-related consulting or vendor support if needed

Background: BuildRight's unified cloud ERP is only as reliable as the data it processes. With 35,000 active SKUs, 600,000+ customer records, 800-1,000 vendors, and 2.8M monthly POS transactions flowing through integrated systems (POS, WMS, ecommerce, procurement, finance), data quality issues propagate rapidly across the enterprise. A duplicate vendor record causes payment errors; an incorrect item master weight causes logistics cost miscalculation; a stale customer address causes delivery failures; an incorrect cost field causes margin reporting errors. This workflow establishes enterprise data governance and ongoing data quality management.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: Data Governance Lead (within IT) review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data quality ownership ambiguity**: without clear Data Steward accountability per domain, data quality issues are "everyone's problem and no one's responsibility"; Data Governance Council must enforce stewardship accountability

- **Remediation vs. operations trade-off**: Data Stewards have data governance responsibilities in addition to their primary operational role; data quality remediation competes with operational priorities

- **Integration data quality cascading**: a data error in Item Master (incorrect weight) cascades through WMS (putaway location), logistics (shipping cost), and finance (landed cost) before detection; upstream quality controls are essential
- **Duplicate proliferation**: without strict duplicate prevention at data entry, duplicates accumulate over time (estimated 3-5% duplicate rate in Customer Master without active dedup per W619)

- **Data quality ROI justification**: data quality investments (tools, stewardship time, remediation projects) compete with other IT and operational priorities for budget; quantifying the cost of poor data quality is essential for business case
Staffing Implication: - **Data Governance Lead** (1 FTE within IT): full-time on data governance framework, monitoring, incident management, and council facilitation. Dedicated role recommended.
- **Data Stewards** (part-time per domain): ~4–8 hours/month per steward on data quality monitoring and remediation. Absorbed within existing functional roles.
- **No incremental headcount** beyond Data Governance Lead.
System Touchpoints: - Data quality monitoring dashboard with automated quality checks
- Master data management (MDM) module per W508
- Integration monitoring per W595 (POS-ERP, ERP-ecommerce, WMS-ERP)
- Data stewardship workflow (issue assignment, remediation tracking)
- Data quality incident log with root cause analysis
- Data governance policy repository per W255
- Internal Audit integration per W359
- Data privacy module per W647
Time Estimate: - Monthly monitoring: 4-6 hours (Data Governance Lead)
- Per incident response: 15 min triage + varies for remediation
- Per impact assessment: 30-60 min
- Daily integration monitoring: 2-3 hours (IT Operations)
- Quarterly council: 2 hours
- Annual audit: 1-2 weeks (Internal Audit)

steps.activity: **Data governance framework**: Data Governance Lead maintains enterprise data governance framework: (a) data domains with assigned Data Stewards: Product Master (Merchandising), Customer Master (CRM), Vendor Master (Procurement), Financial Data (Finance), Employee Data (HR), Location Master (Operations), Transactional Data (IT); (b) data quality dimensions measured per domain: Completeness (are all required fields populated?), Accuracy (does data match real-world values?), Timeliness (is data current?), Consistency (is data consistent across systems?), Uniqueness (are there duplicates?); (c) data quality targets per domain (e.g., Item Master completeness ≥ 98%, Customer Master uniqueness ≥ 99%)

**Monthly data quality monitoring**: Data Governance Lead runs automated data quality checks: (a) Item Master: completeness check (required fields: description, UOM, weight, dimensions, category, cost, price), duplicate detection (same description + same barcode), price reasonableness check (selling price > cost price); (b) Customer Master: duplicate detection (same name + same mobile number or email), completeness check (required fields for loyalty, credit, BIR compliance), inactive account cleanup (no transaction in >24 months); (c) Vendor Master: duplicate detection, completeness check (TIN, banking details, contact information), regulatory compliance fields (BIR 2303 currency per W36); (d) Location Master: address accuracy, operating hours, POS terminal mapping; (e) Financial Data: GL account reconciliation anomalies, intercompany imbalance detection per W442

**Data quality incident response**: when data quality issue is detected (automated alert or user report): (a) classify severity: Critical (financial impact, customer-facing error, compliance violation), High (operational disruption, reporting inaccuracy), Medium (degraded user experience, workflow inefficiency), Low (cosmetic, non-impactful); (b) Critical/High: Data Governance Lead assigns to Data Steward for immediate remediation with SLA (Critical: 4 hours, High: 24 hours); (c) Medium/Low: Data Steward addresses in next monthly cycle; (d) root cause analysis for Critical incidents: was it a data entry error, integration error, system bug, or process gap?; (e) implement preventive control to avoid recurrence

**Master data change impact assessment**: when significant master data changes are proposed: (a) Item Master: new SKU addition, category reclassification, UOM change — assess impact on open POs, inventory balances, pricing rules, planograms per W86, replenishment parameters per W31; (b) Customer Master: account merge/dedup per W619, credit limit change per W145, tier reclassification per W704 — assess impact on open orders, AR balance, loyalty points; (c) Vendor Master: vendor merge, banking detail change, payment terms change — assess impact on open POs, AP balance, contracted pricing; (d) Data Steward documents impact assessment and routes to affected stakeholders before change is executed

**Data integration quality monitoring**: for critical real-time integrations per data-volumes-and-integrations.md: (a) POS to ERP (93,333 transactions/day): monitor transaction completeness (no dropped transactions), price consistency (POS price = ERP price), inventory accuracy (POS deduction = ERP inventory); (b) ERP to Ecommerce (inventory sync every 5 min): monitor sync accuracy (ecommerce stock = ERP stock), price sync accuracy; (c) WMS to ERP (inventory updates <1 min): monitor inventory record consistency; (d) daily reconciliation: compare system counts across integrated systems; (e) alert on integration failures per W595 ERP health check

**Quarterly data governance council**: Data Governance Lead convenes quarterly Data Governance Council: (a) attendees: CIO, Data Stewards (all domains), Compliance, Internal Audit; (b) agenda: data quality scorecard (each domain's quality metrics vs. targets), Critical/High incident review and trend analysis, upcoming regulatory data requirements (BIR e-invoicing, NPC data privacy), data governance policy updates, data stewardship workload and resource needs; (c) decisions: approve data quality target changes, prioritize data remediation projects, approve new data domains or stewards

**Annual data quality audit**: Internal Audit includes data quality in annual audit plan per W359: (a) select sample records from each data domain and verify accuracy against source documents; (b) test data quality controls: duplicate prevention, mandatory field enforcement, approval workflows for changes; (c) test data retention compliance per W256; (d) test data privacy compliance per W647 (customer data access controls, opt-out enforcement); (e) report findings and recommendations to Data Governance Council

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "Daily exception monitoring" (replaces manual Step 1).

Background: Existing LP workflows (W79, W80, W267-W269) cover physical security, access control, and cash management procedures. W681 covers DC quality control. However, no workflow addresses the systematic use of data analytics to detect, investigate, and reduce shrinkage — which includes theft (internal and external), vendor fraud, administrative errors, and damage. For a PHP 62.3B revenue retailer, even a 0.5% improvement in shrinkage rate represents PHP 311M in recovered margin.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: Loss Prevention Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **False positives**: analytics-generated exception reports may flag legitimate transactions (voids due to customer changing mind, high-value transactions during construction season); excessive false positives erode investigator trust in the system

- **CCTV retention limitations**: most stores retain CCTV footage for 30-90 days per W256; investigations for slow-building patterns (e.g., systematic small thefts over months) may lack visual evidence for early periods

- **Internal theft sensitivity**: investigating employees for theft requires sensitivity and due process; wrongful accusation creates legal liability (illegal dismissal per Philippine labor law) and employee relations damage; evidence must be strong before confrontation

- **Organized retail crime**: professional theft rings targeting high-value hardware items (power tools, copper wire) operate across multiple stores and regions; requires coordinated investigation across stores and collaboration with PNP

- **LP technology cost**: advanced LP technologies (AI-powered CCTV analytics, RFID, exception-based reporting platforms) represent significant investment; ROI must be demonstrated through measurable shrinkage reduction
Staffing Implication: - **Loss Prevention Manager** (1 FTE at HQ): full-time on LP program management and investigation oversight.
- **LP Analyst** (1-2 FTE at HQ): full-time on daily exception monitoring, analytics, and investigation support.
- **Store Managers**: ~2–4 hours/month on store-level investigation support and LP awareness. Absorbed within existing role.
- **No incremental headcount** beyond LP Manager and Analyst.
System Touchpoints: - POS exception-based reporting (EBR) module (POS-085)
- Inventory shrinkage analytics (cycle count variance analysis per W6)
- LP case management system
- CCTV management system with analytics integration
- Transaction log analysis tool
- HR disciplinary integration per W152
- Vendor management integration per W44/W706
- Insurance claims management
- BI dashboard for LP analytics reporting
- W691 technology scouting integration for LP technology evaluation
Time Estimate: - Daily exception review: 1-2 hours
- Weekly analytics: 2-3 hours
- Per investigation case: 6-12 hours total
- Monthly reporting: 4-6 hours
- Program management: 8-12 hours/month

steps.activity: **Daily exception monitoring**: LP Analyst reviews automated exception reports from POS and inventory systems: (a) POS void exceptions: high void rates by cashier, voids after large transactions, manager override frequency; (b) refund exceptions: high refund amounts, refund without merchandise return, refunds to same customer frequently; (c) discount exceptions: unauthorized discounts, excessive discount usage, employee discount abuse; (d) inventory exceptions: negative inventory alerts (selling items not in stock per system), receiving quantity variances (PO quantity vs. GR quantity); (e) transaction anomalies: unusually high average transaction value, sweet-hearting patterns (repeated scanning avoidance)

**Weekly shrinkage analytics**: LP Analyst generates weekly shrinkage analytics report: (a) shrinkage by store: actual shrinkage (from cycle count per W6) vs. target; identify top 20 shrinkage stores; (b) shrinkage by category: which product categories have highest shrinkage (typically power tools, electrical fittings, adhesives — high-value, pocketable items); (c) shrinkage trend: compare to prior week, prior month, same period last year; (d) correlation analysis: shrinkage vs. staffing levels, shrinkage vs. traffic volume, shrinkage vs. LP incident reports; (e) automated alert: stores exceeding shrinkage threshold (>2% of revenue for the period) flagged for investigation

**Investigation initiation**: when analytics identify suspicious patterns: (a) LP Analyst opens investigation case: case number, store, suspected type (internal theft, external theft, vendor fraud, administrative error), estimated loss amount, supporting data (exception reports, transaction logs, CCTV timestamps); (b) classify investigation: Routine (estimated loss <PHP 50K), Major (PHP 50K-500K), Critical (>PHP 500K or organized pattern); (c) Routine: LP Analyst investigates with Store Manager; Major: Loss Prevention Manager leads investigation with Internal Audit support; Critical: COO + Legal + HR involved

**Evidence gathering**: for active investigations: (a) POS transaction log analysis: detailed review of flagged transactions, pattern identification across dates and cashiers; (b) inventory movement audit: trace inventory from receiving per W3 through putaway, sales, and adjustments per W91/W92; (c) CCTV review: for physical stores, review relevant camera footage (retention per W256 — typically 30-90 days); (d) vendor delivery documentation review: verify GR quantities match vendor documentation per W3; (e) digital evidence preservation: screenshots, data exports, and CCTV clips stored per W255 with chain-of-custody documentation for potential legal proceedings

**Investigation conclusion and action**: (a) if internal theft confirmed: HR initiates disciplinary process per W152, with Legal review for criminal complaint if warranted; recover losses through salary deduction (per Philippine labor law limits) or civil action; (b) if external theft confirmed: coordinate with local PNP, file criminal complaint with evidence; adjust store security measures per W79; (c) if vendor fraud confirmed: Procurement initiates vendor action per W44/W706 (penalty, de-listing per W36); recover losses through vendor chargeback per W88; (d) if administrative error: implement corrective process and training per W655; (e) all case outcomes documented in LP case management system for trend analysis

**Monthly LP analytics reporting**: Loss Prevention Manager presents monthly report to COO and CFO: (a) total shrinkage: actual vs. target by region, by store, by category; (b) shrinkage as % of revenue trend; (c) investigation case summary: cases opened, closed, by type, by store; (d) recovery: amount recovered through investigations, vendor chargebacks, insurance claims; (e) LP investment ROI: cost of LP operations vs. shrinkage reduction achieved; (f) recommendations: store-level LP improvements, category-specific security measures, policy changes

**Shrinkage reduction program management**: Loss Prevention Manager manages ongoing shrinkage reduction initiatives: (a) high-theft category protection: locked display cases for power tools, spider wraps for electronics, EAS tags for high-value items; (b) store layout optimization: camera coverage gaps, blind spots, high-theft category placement near staffed areas; (c) vendor delivery audit program: random receiving audits per W681 for high-shrinkage vendors; (d) employee awareness training: include LP awareness in W51 training curriculum; (e) technology evaluation: evaluate new LP technologies (RFID, AI-powered CCTV analytics, exception-based reporting enhancements) via W691 technology scouting

workflows.name: ERP User Access Quarterly Review, Segregation of Duties (SoD) Audit & Excessive Access Remediation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "System generates quarterly access review report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews SoD conflict report" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-distribute of "distributes access certification lists to Department Heads" (replaces manual Step 3).
Background: BuildRight's unified ERP system spans financial transactions, payroll, inventory, POS, ecommerce, and HR across 5 legal entities. With ~6,762 users, the risk of excessive access, Segregation of Duties (SoD) violations, and orphaned accounts is significant. SoD violations — where a single user can perform incompatible functions (e.g., create a vendor and approve payment, or process a refund and authorize a void) — create fraud risk and internal control weaknesses. Philippine regulatory requirements (BIR CAS compliance, SEC reporting, NPC data privacy) all require demonstrable access controls. CTL-46 (Internal Controls Matrix) mandates quarterly user access reviews.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Department Head certification fatigue**: with 200 Store Managers + 30+ HQ Department Heads, achieving 100% certification completion within 10 business days is challenging; Store Managers may rubber-stamp certifications without careful review

- **Emergency access accumulation**: employees who received temporary elevated access for emergencies (W60 emergency procurement, system outages) may retain elevated permissions after the emergency resolves; temporary access grants are difficult to track without automated expiration

- **SoD mitigating controls vs. true remediation**: Department Heads may request "mitigating controls" (monitoring, dual approval) instead of removing conflicting roles; while acceptable under some audit frameworks, this shifts risk from prevention to detection

- **Cross-entity access complexity**: with 5 legal entities in the same ERP instance, a user may have appropriate access in one entity but excessive access in another; entity-level access filtering adds complexity
Staffing Implication: - IT Security Manager: ~7 hours/quarter on access review; primary responsibility; absorbed
- System Administrator: ~2 hours/quarter executing changes; absorbed
- Department Heads/Store Managers: ~1 hour/quarter each; ~230 hours/quarter total; absorbed (part of management responsibility)
- Internal Auditor: ~4 hours/quarter; absorbed
- No incremental headcount
System Touchpoints: - Automated access review report: user accounts, roles, permissions, last login, SoD conflicts, orphaned accounts, dormant accounts, privileged accounts (W1408.1)

- SoD conflict engine: configurable rule set defining incompatible role pairs (e.g., AP + Payment, JE + Approval, Vendor Create + PO Approve); real-time prevention of new SoD violations during role assignment (W152) + quarterly detective review (W1408.2)
- Department Head access certification portal: list of reports with current roles, certification buttons, and comment fields (W1408.3)
- Access modification workflow: IT Security Manager approval + System Administrator execution with audit trail (W1408.5–6)

- Integration with W152 (IT provisioning — role assignment source), W292 (employee master — active/separated status), W43 (separation — account deactivation trigger), W37 (loss prevention — fraud investigation access), W261 (internal audit — access review as audit evidence), CTL-46 (internal controls matrix — quarterly review control)
Time Estimate: - Report generation: automated (~5 min)
- IT Security Manager review: ~4 hours/quarter
- Department Head certification: ~1 hour × ~230 certifiers = ~230 hours/quarter
- Access modification processing: ~6 hours/quarter
- Internal Auditor review: ~4 hours/quarter
- DPO review: ~2 hours/quarter
- Summary report: ~1 hour/quarter
- Total quarterly: ~250 hours/quarter (~80 hours/month)

steps.activity: System generates quarterly access review report: (a) list of all active user accounts with assigned roles, permissions, and last login date; (b) SoD conflict report — identifies users with incompatible role combinations (e.g., AP Clerk + Payment Approver, Store Manager + System Administrator, Payroll Officer + HR Master Data Editor); (c) excessive access report — identifies users with permissions beyond their job requirements (based on role template comparison); (d) orphaned account report — accounts active for employees who have separated (cross-referenced with HR employee master W292); (e) dormant account report — accounts with no login in 90+ days; (f) privileged account report — users with system administrator, database administrator, or superuser roles

IT Security Manager reviews SoD conflict report; classifies each conflict as: (a) **Critical** — financial transaction risk (e.g., vendor creation + payment, journal entry + approval, refund processing + void authorization); (b) **High** — data integrity risk (e.g., inventory adjustment + approval, price override + POS admin); (c) **Medium** — operational risk (e.g., report generation across entities, read access to HR data outside department)

IT Security Manager distributes access certification lists to Department Heads: each Department Head receives a list of their direct and indirect reports with current ERP roles and permissions; Department Head must certify that each employee's access is appropriate for their current job function; mark each as "Certified — Access Appropriate" or "Action Required — Reduce/Modify Access"

Department Heads return certified access lists within 10 business days; IT Security Manager compiles responses; follows up with non-responsive Department Heads (escalation to VP after 15 business days)

IT Security Manager processes access modifications: (a) **Orphaned accounts** — immediately disabled and flagged for HR confirmation of separation; (b) **Critical SoD conflicts** — one of the conflicting roles removed within 2 business days; user and Department Head notified; if business justification requires both roles, mitigating control documented (e.g., enhanced transaction monitoring); (c) **Excessive access** — permissions reduced to role template standard; (d) **Dormant accounts** — disabled if confirmed as inactive; if employee on leave, flagged for reactivation upon return
System Administrator executes access changes in ERP; system logs all modifications with IT Security Manager approval; change log stored for 10 years per BIR CAS requirements

Internal Auditor reviews quarterly access review results: verifies SoD conflicts were remediated, orphaned accounts were disabled, Department Head certifications were completed; samples 10% of remediated accounts for independent verification; includes findings in quarterly internal audit report (W21.1)

DPO reviews privileged access to personal data (customer records, employee records, payroll data): verifies that only authorized personnel with documented business need have access to PII; documents findings in NPC-required privacy impact assessment

IT Security Manager generates quarterly access review summary for CIO: total accounts reviewed, SoD conflicts found and remediated, orphaned accounts disabled, Department Head certification completion rate, overdue certifications, and trend comparison to prior quarters

Background: BuildRight's unified ERP system supports 200 stores, 4 DCs, and HQ with near-real-time POS event streaming, ecommerce integration, warehouse management, payroll, and financial operations. Any change to the production system — configuration modification, software patch (W495), integration update, report change, or workflow adjustment — carries the risk of disrupting store operations, payment processing, or supply chain execution. The Change Advisory Board (CAB) provides structured risk assessment and approval governance for all changes before they reach production, ensuring that changes are properly tested, communicated, and scheduled to minimize business disruption.
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: behaves differently after a change
Pain Points / Risks: - **CAB bottleneck for urgent business changes**: weekly CAB cadence means a normal CR submitted on Thursday waits until next Wednesday for review; business-critical changes (e.g., new promotional pricing configuration error needing immediate fix) may be forced through the emergency path, undermining CAB governance

- **Store Manager communication gaps**: high-risk changes require 48-hour advance communication to Store Managers; Store Managers may not read communications in time, leading to confusion when a system behaves differently after a change

- **Change-related incidents in 200-store environment**: a change that affects POS behavior (e.g., new barcode format handling, payment terminal integration update) has 600 POS terminals as potential failure points; rollback of a POS change requires touching all 600 terminals

- **Insufficient test environment parity**: the staging environment may not perfectly replicate production data volume (2.8M POS transactions/month); a change that passes testing may still fail at production scale
Staffing Implication: - IT Change Manager: ~10–12 hours/week on CAB-related activities; primary governance responsibility; absorbed by IT Manager or dedicated change management role
- CAB Members: ~1–2 hours/week each for CAB meeting + CR review; 6 members × 1.5 hours = ~9 hours/week total; absorbed by existing IT and business roles
- No incremental headcount
System Touchpoints: - IT Service Management (ITSM) system: Change Request submission, classification, risk assessment, workflow routing (W1409.1–3)
- CAB meeting workspace: CR queue with risk classification, testing evidence, impact assessment (W1409.4)
- Maintenance window calendar: blocked time slots for production deployments with store notification integration (W1409.5)
- Emergency CAB communication channel: instant virtual meeting or chat channel with minimum quorum (W1409.6)
- Post-implementation monitoring: incident queue filtered by change ID with 48-hour monitoring window (W1409.7)
- CAB effectiveness dashboard: CR volume, approval rate, change success rate, emergency change frequency, lead time (W1409.8)

- Integration with W495 (ERP patch management — patch CRs routed to CAB), W73 (system upgrade testing — test evidence for CRs), W132 (software development — code changes require CAB approval for production), W152 (user provisioning — Standard change path), W48 (helpdesk — change-related incident detection), W380 (event management — deployment event monitoring)
Time Estimate: - CR submission: ~30 min/CR × 10 CRs/week = ~5 hours/week (distributed across IT staff)
- IT Change Manager CR review: ~15 min/CR × 10 CRs = ~2.5 hours/week
- CAB meeting: ~60–90 min/week
- High-risk change additional effort: ~2–4 hours × ~2/week = ~4–8 hours/week

- Monthly report: ~1 hour/month

steps.activity: Change requestor submits Change Request (CR) in IT Service Management system: (a) description of change, (b) business justification, (c) affected ERP modules and integration points, (d) impacted locations (stores, DCs, HQ), (e) proposed implementation date/time, (f) rollback plan, (g) testing evidence (from test environment per W73), (h) communication plan for affected users; system auto-classifies CR as Standard (pre-approved template), Normal (requires CAB review), or Emergency (expedited approval path)
steps.r: Change Requestor (IT staff or business user)

steps.activity: **Standard changes** (pre-approved templates: e.g., new user creation per W152, store opening configuration per W16, report parameter changes): IT Change Manager auto-approves without CAB review; change proceeds directly to implementation scheduling

**Normal changes**: system queues CR for next weekly CAB meeting; IT Change Manager reviews CR for completeness and assigns risk assessment category: (a) **Low Risk**: cosmetic changes, report formatting, non-critical configuration; (b) **Medium Risk**: workflow rule changes, new integration endpoints, form modifications; (c) **High Risk**: ERP module updates, POS system changes, payment integration changes, financial close configuration, database schema changes, security configuration

**CAB weekly meeting** (Wednesday, 60–90 min): IT Change Manager presents all queued normal CRs to CAB members; for each CR: (a) change requestor presents technical details and testing results, (b) Business Representative assesses impact on store operations, financial close, or supply chain, (c) IT Security Manager assesses security impact, (d) CAB discusses implementation timing (prefer Sunday 2:00 AM–6:00 AM maintenance window to avoid POS and store impact), (e) CAB votes: Approve / Approve with Conditions / Reject / Defer for more information

**High-Risk changes**: require additional controls: (a) mandatory weekend maintenance window (Saturday 10 PM – Sunday 6 AM), (b) staging environment deployment and 48-hour soak test before production, (c) pre-deployment communication to all affected Store Managers (via store communication app) 48 hours in advance, (d) IT Infrastructure Lead on standby during and after deployment, (e) automated smoke test of critical functions (POS transaction processing, inventory sync, payment gateway, ecommerce order flow) within 1 hour of deployment, (f) 24-hour monitoring period with hourly health checks
steps.r: IT Change Manager / IT Infrastructure Lead

steps.activity: **Emergency changes** (production outage or critical defect): IT Change Manager convenes emergency CAB within 2 hours (virtual meeting or chat channel); minimum 3 CAB members required (IT Change Manager, IT Infrastructure Lead, IT Security Manager); emergency CR approved with conditions: (a) fix deployed immediately, (b) retrospective documentation completed within 24 hours, (c) root cause analysis per W378 within 5 business days, (d) full CAB review of emergency change at next weekly meeting

Post-implementation: change requestor confirms successful deployment; IT Service Desk Lead monitors incident queue for 48 hours for any issues related to the change; if issues detected: IT Change Manager initiates rollback per CR rollback plan

Monthly: IT Change Manager generates CAB effectiveness report: (a) total CRs submitted, approved, rejected, deferred, (b) % of changes implemented on schedule, (c) % of changes causing incidents (change-related incidents), (d) emergency change frequency and root causes, (e) average CR lead time from submission to implementation, (f) CAB meeting attendance rate; report submitted to CIO

workflows.name: Enterprise Release Calendar & Peak-Season Change-Freeze Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Release-calendar collisions auto-detected when the three change engines publish entries (replaces manual Step 2 reconciliation).
- Freeze-window entry/exit auto-broadcast to store and regional channels (VS-63) (replaces manual Step 3 notifications).
Controls: - CTL-322 (ensure controlled execution — Service Management (PA-27.1).)
- operational: freeze exceptions require CAB risk assessment (W1409) with Store Operations sign-off
- operational: the release calendar is CIO-approved before publication
Pain Points / Risks: - **Peak-window risk**: a poorly-timed store-facing release degrades 12.12 trading; mitigated by the published freeze calendar and the CAB exception gate with Store Operations sign-off (Step 4)
- **Shadow-change risk**: urgent fixes bypass the freeze and collide with peak hotfixes; mitigated by the emergency-CAB path (W1409) and the post-peak review of unauthorized changes
- **Backlog-surge risk**: deferred work floods the post-peak window and forces risky batching; mitigated by the staggered flush plan (Step 5)
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the existing IT change-management role (W132/W1409 operator); no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Shared release-calendar workspace published to the CAB (W1409), the ERP monthly train (W495), the SEP ring dashboard (W5517) and patch management (W367)
- Seasonal calendar master (W306); W595 Tier-1 health dashboards; hypercare rota (VS-134)
- Store/regional communications channel (VS-63); exception log in the change-management system (W132/W1409)
Time Estimate: Calendar publication ≈ 24 hours/year; reconciliation 2 hours × 12 ≈ 24 hours/year; freeze-window operations 4 hours/week × ~16 weeks ≈ 64 hours/year; exceptions 1 hour × ~30 ≈ 30 hours/year; flush planning 8 hours × 2 peaks ≈ 16 hours/year; post-peak review ≈ 8 hours/year. Total **≈ 166 hours/year** (≈0.08 FTE), absorbed within the IT change-management function.

steps.activity: **Annual freeze-calendar publication**: Map freeze windows onto the merchandising peak calendar (ber-months build-up, 11.11/12.12, payday weekends, Warehouse Sale, Holy Week) using the seasonal master (W306); publish to all change engines

**Monthly cross-train reconciliation**: Align the ERP monthly train (W495), the built-product ring dashboard (W5517) and infrastructure/store patch cycles (W367) onto the single release calendar; resolve collisions
**Freeze-entry readiness gate**: Per window — Tier-1 system health (W595), support staffing & hypercare rota (VS-134), rollback plans on file, freeze communications to stores/regional teams (VS-63)
steps.r: IT Change Mgr / Service Desk Lead

steps.activity: **Exception adjudication**: Business-critical/emergency changes during freeze via CAB risk assessment (W1409) with Store Operations sign-off for store-facing changes; log and report exceptions
**Freeze-exit & backlog flush**: Sequence the deferred backlog post-peak; stagger high-risk releases to avoid a risky batch landing
**Post-peak review**: Incident/change-failure review feeding W378 problem management and next-year calendar adjustments
steps.r: IT Change Mgr / Service Desk Lead
